Clarity.justification: The paper follows a logical structure with clear sections (Abstract, Introduction, Related Work, Method, Experiments, Discussion). Ideas such as the graph encoding schema and LayerNorm gauge-fixing hypothesis are articulated explicitly. However, clarity is reduced by lengthy defensive caveats, repeated mentions of single-seed limitations, training-duration confounds, and unverified citations that interrupt the narrative flow.

Novelty.justification: The core claim (graph-based permutation-equivariant SSL enables CNN-to-ViT zero-shot transfer) directly extends prior supervised results from Kofinas et al. (ICLR 2024) and Kalogeropoulos et al. (NeurIPS 2024). The negative finding on scale equivariance and the speculative LayerNorm gauge-fixing hypothesis add incremental insight, but the work does not introduce fundamentally new architectures, objectives, or theoretical bounds.

Soundness.justification: Multiple critical flaws exist: all cross-architecture R² values derive from a single training seed with only 53 ViT models (degenerate p-values reported as 0.5); the h-m2 ablation compares 50-epoch vs 100-epoch checkpoints, confounding symmetry-group effects; MMD is misused because SANE collapse artificially lowers the metric; the graph decoder reconstructs edge statistics rather than functional weights, yielding exactly chance accuracy (0.100) on interpolation; several experimental gates failed (STOP instead of PASS) and synthetic data appear in logs. These issues render the empirical claims unreliable.

Significance.justification: The topic (cross-architecture weight-space transfer) is relevant to the workshop theme, yet the combination of single-seed statistics, small test set, decoder failure, and methodological confounds severely limits the reliability and potential impact of the reported findings. The work is unlikely to influence subsequent research without substantial additional validation.

strengths: Clear articulation of the graph encoding schema versus flat tokenization
Explicit reporting of limitations and single-seed nature of results
weaknesses: Single-seed evaluation with n=53 and degenerate statistical tests
Training-duration confound and decoder producing random weights (acc=0.100)
